Legal, finance and accounting

Jobs in this route, and the maths they use.

Percentages

Payroll administrator

Legal, finance and accounting

\(\displaystyle \text{tax} = 0.2(\text{pay} - \text{allowance})\)

How much tax comes off a £2,500 month?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Payroll works out the tax taken from each month's pay. In 2026 to 2027 the first £12,570 a year is tax-free and the next band is taxed at 20%. Someone earns £2,500 this month (example figure). National Insurance is worked out separately. Real payslips use HMRC's tax tables, so they can differ by a few pence.

  1. Tax-free each month: \(12570 \div 12 = \pounds 1{,}047.50\).
  2. Taxed: \(2500 - 1047.50 = \pounds 1{,}452.50\).
  3. Tax: \(20\% \text{ of } 1452.50 = 0.2 \times 1452.50 = \pounds 290.50\).

The answer: \(0.2 \times 1452.50 = \pounds 290.50\) tax

Bookkeeper

Legal, finance and accounting

\(\displaystyle \text{VAT due} = 0.2S - 0.2P\)

S is sales, P is purchases, before VAT

How much does this business owe HMRC?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Every three months a business tells HMRC the VAT it charged customers and the VAT it paid suppliers, and pays the difference. Sales of £45,000 and purchases of £15,000 this quarter, before VAT, all at 20% (example figures).

  1. VAT charged: \(0.2 \times 45000 = \pounds 9{,}000\).
  2. VAT paid: \(0.2 \times 15000 = \pounds 3{,}000\).
  3. To pay HMRC: \(9000 - 3000 = \pounds 6{,}000\).

The answer: \(9000 - 3000 = \pounds 6{,}000\) to HMRC
